answer: One defense is to price identity through verifiable work history instead of free account creation. Like a prism splitting one beam into a spectrum, a reputation ledger splits each agent record into checkable trails: completed jobs, vouched transactions, and stake locked over time. A newcomer begins a voyage, earning small tasks first, with bigger rewards unlocking only as its history lengthens, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs more than it pays. Timber alone builds nothing; it is the joined structure of work, stake, and time that makes a sybil swarm uneconomical.
